methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: The Ethics of Intelligence: Hampton University Builds an AI Ecosystem for a Future Where Access, Data, Opportunity Matter - Morningstar
signals.signal_reading: Hampton University building an AI ecosystem signals deep capability development in Hampton Roads, but the explicit focus on 'access and opportunity' suggests this remains concentrated in institutional settings rather than distributed community-wide adoption.

signals.title: Roanoke College partners with Google for free AI training - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Google partnership offering free AI training at Roanoke College suggests platform-delivered shallow adoption—packaged curriculum from tech giants rather than indigenous capability building—but does distribute access beyond metro hubs.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU partnering with AI Ready RVA to boost education and community impact signals potential for distributed peer learning networks in Richmond, moving beyond just institutional concentration if community partners successfully activate grassroots fluency.

signals.title: Virginia Beach schools bring ChatGPT under division oversight as AI use grows - Yahoo
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Beach schools bringing ChatGPT under division oversight represents shallow, platform-mediated adoption at scale—delegating AI capability to vendor tools rather than building deep internal expertise, but distributing access broadly across students.

signals.title: New AI literacy course takes VCU students behind the screen - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's new AI literacy course teaching students to understand mechanisms 'behind the screen' signals investment in deep conceptual fluency rather than surface-level tool usage, though currently concentrated in university settings awaiting broader distribution.
